updates.update_type: existing maritime drawer correction / source revision preservation
updates.finding: Reuters' current Sep. 21 report gives 17 trackable commodity-vessel transits through Hormuz over the weekend, versus 37 the prior weekend. Sunday had five exits and two entries; Saturday had eight exits and two entries. This differs from the 12-versus-35 denominator preserved in the midnight sweep from an earlier Reuters/Kpler version. Preserve both publication-state observations and supersede the earlier denominator for current use rather than rewriting the prior artifact. Reuters also reports transponder-dark traffic.
updates.status: SUPPORTED REVISED COMMERCIAL-DATA DENOMINATOR; PRIOR REUTERS VERSION PRESERVED
updates.drawer_effect: Supersede 12/35 as the current Reuters/Kpler weekend denominator with 17/37; retain the midnight artifact as evidence of the earlier published value.

updates.update_type: existing Hormuz energy-flow drawer update / commercial logistics adaptation
updates.finding: Reuters energy analysis citing Kpler reports Hormuz oil exports around 6.5 million bpd so far in September, highest since the brief post-June-ceasefire spike. About 2.5 million bpd is expected to be loaded through ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman in September versus 1.4 million bpd in August, roughly 40% of current Hormuz-moving volume. Shuttle tankers transit the strait, often dark, then transfer crude south of Hormuz to onward carriers. Reuters reports a narrow Omani-coast corridor under U.S. naval protection. VLCC Gulf-to-China freight exceeds $30/barrel in cited LSEG data.
updates.status: SUPPORTED COMMERCIAL-DATA ADAPTATION; NOT NORMALIZED FREEDOM OF NAVIGATION
updates.drawer_effect: Add logistics-mechanism evidence explaining why export volumes can recover while visible transit counts and normal navigation remain severely degraded. Treat Reuters Open Interest interpretation separately from underlying Kpler/LSEG figures.

updates.finding: Current Reuters/Kpler data reports 22 tankers carrying 42 million barrels exited Hormuz in the week of Sep. 13, with Saudi Arabia and Iraq each accounting for 43% of volume. Reuters reports no visible Saudi oil loadings at Yanbu since Sep. 16. A separate Reuters market report cites satellite data showing Saudi oil through Hormuz averaging 2.9 million bpd over the prior six days versus 0.7 million bpd in August.
updates.status: SUPPORTED REROUTING/DISPOSITION UPDATE; PIPELINE REPAIR NOT ESTABLISHED
updates.drawer_effect: Strengthen evidence of Saudi fallback to Hormuz and continuing Yanbu impairment; do not infer East-West pipeline repair from recovered exports.

updates.update_type: existing Qatar energy/infrastructure drawer BDA and repair-status update
updates.finding: QatarEnergy CEO Saad al-Kaabi said attacks on Ras Laffan wiped out 17% of Qatar LNG capacity, damaged two LNG trains whose repairs could take three years, and damaged one GTL plant expected to complete repairs in Q1 2027. He said QatarEnergy is producing very little LNG and that normal gas operations could resume within weeks after Hormuz reopens. Equipment for North Field East expansion remains unable to reach Qatar through disrupted Hormuz; later NFE trains may be delayed. Qatar rejected proposed pipeline alternatives through neighboring states on commercial and technical grounds.
updates.status: SUPPORTED OPERATOR-ATTRIBUTED BDA/REPAIR ESTIMATE; LONG-TERM PROJECT IMPACT CONDITIONAL
updates.drawer_effect: Update Ras Laffan BDA and repair horizons; separate operator repair estimate from independent physical BDA and separate current damage from conditional expansion delay.

updates.finding: Five Yemeni military sources told Reuters Houthi forces were seeking the Kahboub Mountains in Taiz and Lahij, strategic heights separating their newly seized Red Sea coast from government-held southern areas. Fighting centered near Al-Wazi'iyah and Ras al-Ara. Reuters reports the Houthis already seized Yemen's Red Sea coast this month; Saudi strikes have not yet dislodged them from the described advance. The territorial push threatens to consolidate Houthi leverage around Bab el-Mandeb but does not by itself establish physical closure of the strait.
updates.status: SUPPORTED MULTI-SOURCE MILITARY DISPOSITION; STRAIT CLOSURE NOT ESTABLISHED
updates.drawer_effect: Update Houthi territorial disposition and preserve distinction between control of adjacent terrain/islands and control or closure of international navigation.

updates.update_type: existing Yemen human-impact drawer denominator update
updates.finding: Reuters reports the United Nations now puts the renewed Yemen flare-up at nearly 700 killed, thousands injured, nearly 130,000 internally displaced, and more than 3,000 people fleeing by boat across the Red Sea to Africa. This supersedes the Sep. 15 UNHCR denominator of over 100,000 internally displaced for current use while preserving the earlier observation date.
updates.drawer_effect: Supersede the prior displacement denominator for current status; retain earlier series for chronology.

updates.finding: Reuters reports Saudi-backed Yemeni president Rashad al-Alimi requested U.S. military help in a Sunday call with President Trump; two sources said Trump made no direct pledge. Reuters separately reports the New York Times claim that U.S. strikes on Houthis were prepared and called off at the last minute, but Reuters could not independently verify that strike-order/cancellation account and CENTCOM referred questions to the White House.
updates.status: SUPPORT REQUEST CORROBORATED; NO U.S. PLEDGE REPORTED; STRIKE-ORDER/CANCELLATION CLAIM UNVERIFIED BY REUTERS
updates.drawer_effect: Add direct Yemeni request and reported non-commitment; preserve NYT strike-preparation story as attributed/unverified rather than fact.
